answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to earn endorsements from already-trusted peers over time, like a willow's roots spreading slowly through the soil. Newcomers gain higher transaction limits only after sustained, useful work. One onyx-hard rule anchors it: no account may vouch for more newcomers than its own reputation supports, and vouchers lose staked reputation if their invitees turn out to be sable-shadow duplicates of one operator.
